title: Possible combinations: 12 lowercase letters vs 8 full-mix characters

source.name: Character-set sizes from Hive Systems' Password Table methodology
source.publisher: Hive Systems (character-set definitions); arithmetic is exact

notes: Simple combinatorics: a 12-character password using only the 26 lowercase letters has 26^12 = ~95.4 quadrillion possible combinations. An 8-character password using the full 94-character keyboard set (upper, lower, digits, symbols) has 94^8 = ~6.1 quadrillion. The longer, simpler password has roughly 15.6x more combinations despite a far smaller alphabet.
